acceptanceCriteria: impact and test-validity JSON receipts carry a producer object with version, build and commit, with a stated value when a field is unknown.
Release installs report a non-zero build in --version, or the spec states why build 0 is correct and how consumers identify the build.
Spec requirements and tests cover a dev build and a release-stamped build.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1300 (opened 2026-10-20). Feature request; not yet specified. **Observed.** `corvint impact` and `corvint test-validity` JSON name no producer version, build or commit. `corvint --version` prints `Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 0)` for an installed release build, so a consumer that must label each derived item with the producing build has to infer it from the install directory name. **Wanted.** A `producer` object in every receipt (`version`, `build`, `commit`), and a non-zero build in `--version` for release installs. **Why.** Consumers that cache or cite receipts cannot tell which build produced them, and cross-build comparisons are unverifiable. See beamfall/corvint#1300 for the full text.
title: Machine-readable receipts carry no producer build identity (issue #1300)
